 by CORY SMITH | The National News Desk
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:32 PM Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images, file Comment on this story 0 Comment Share story Share (TNND) — Affordable Care Act health insurance open enrollment begins Sunday amid sharply rising costs and a shuffling of carriers.
 "You have to really shop around and look around and know what you're getting yourself into," warned Simon Haeder, an associate professor of public health at Ohio State University.
 He said ACA plans can feature big changes even when they’re called the same thing as they were last year. Pharmacy benefits, provider networks and more could be different.
 Health policy organization KFF says nearly a dozen carriers have announced they will exit the ACA marketplaces in the coming plan year.
 Meanwhile, seven carriers have announced they will enter new state marketplaces, according to KFF.
 A KFF tracker , alongside the Peterson Center on Healthcare, says ACA marketplace premiums are expected to go up a median of 15% next year.
 A new analysis from The Washington Post came up with the same projection. The Post analysis says 2027 rates have been finalized in 37 states and Washington, D.C.
 The Peterson-KFF Health System Tracker said the 15% increase would come on the heels of a 20% median rate change this year.
 Haeder said ACA, or Obamacare, enrollees face the “double whammy” of rising premiums and reduced subsidies.
 Enhanced ACA subsidies expired at the end of 2025. They were introduced in 2021’s American Rescue Plan and extended through last year as part of 2022’s Inflation Reduction Act.
 The enhanced subsidies helped fuel a surge in ACA enrollment, which topped out during the 2025 plan year at around 24 million people after having plateaued at around 10.5 million in the years before the pandemic.
 Enrollment dropped this year as costs increased.
 Plan sign-ups fell by over a million during last year’s enrollment period , with the expiration of the enhanced subsidies still on the horizon.
 And there’s evidence that ACA coverage dwindled as the year went on, with some enrollees stopping payments after Congress failed to come through with an extension to the enhanced subsidies.
 Another KFF report found that enrollment in the individual health insurance market fell 18% between June 2025 and June 2026 . That included some off-exchange enrollment, but KFF said the bulk of it was ACA marketplace coverage. 
 “The subsidies are gone. We know this. That's kind of factored in. People know this at this point,” Haeder said. “I think mostly the prices are going up again, similar range as last year, which creates a situation (where) you reflect, ‘What can I afford in my life? How sick am I?’ If you're really sick, you're diabetic, you have cancer, you're going to stay in the plan. If you're healthier, you're dropping out.”
 SEE ALSO: White House says more than 760,000 Obamacare accounts are fraudulent 
 ACA enrollees with incomes between 100% and 400% of the poverty level may qualify for subsidies . But healthier people with higher incomes might find it harder to justify the cost of signing up again in 2027.
 The more healthy people that drop out, the higher the risk for insurers. And that likely exerts upward pressure on health premiums for everyone still enrolled.
 Dec. 15 is the last day under the federal exchange to enroll and get coverage beginning Jan. 1. Open enrollment ends Jan. 15 for coverage starting Feb. 1.
 View post on X 
 Open enrollment can vary for state exchanges. California's exchange keeps enrollment open until Jan. 31, for example.
 Haeder said people should sign up through the official government sites, either HealthCare.gov or the state-based exchanges. That’s the best way to avoid getting scammed.
 Federally certified navigators can help consumers find affordable coverage that meets their needs and assist them beyond the enrollment process. Find a state-by-state list here .
 HealthCare.gov also features a ZIP code search for local help from an agent, broker or assister.
